title.narrative: Safe Access to Fuel and Energy Plus - Fas 2
Safe Access to Fuel and Energy Plus - Phase 2

description.narrative:
Goal: Refugee and host communities will become more climate-resilient, and food secure as well as less exposed to sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) and disaster risks through sustained access to cleaner cooking energy, improved natural resource management and green skills development and livelihoods.
Objective 1: "Access to Cleaner Energy" will focus on provision of cleaner and more efficient cooking energy sources through the continued provision of LPG and energy efficient cooking equipment to reduce deforestation and mitigate climate change.
Objective 2: "Environment and Ecosystems" will focus on knowledge management related to watershed and natural resources management and climate action, ecosystem rehabilitation and environmental conservation to strengthen community resilience to mitigate conflicts over natural resources, disaster and climate shocks such as landslide risks, floods, and droughts through Nature-Based Solutions, as well as synergies with green livelihoods, environmental awareness and strengthening social cohesion between host and refugee communities.
Objective 3: "Resilience" will contribute to strengthening resilience and existing livelihoods capacities while preventing further harm to the environment due to the negative coping strategies and unsustainable agriculture practices. It will similarly ensure interventions in the camps are environmentally sound and refugees can be as self-sufficient as possible.

Den första fasen av SAFE+ avslutades officiellt i juni 2022. I samråd med Bangladeshs regering, givare och fyra FN-organ (UNHCR, IOM, WFP och FAO) har en andra fas av det gemensamma FN-programmet utvecklats för att upprätthålla de goda resultat som uppnåtts av SAFE+ efter 2022. Målet med programmet är för flyktingar och värdsamhällen att bli mer klimattåliga och matsäkra samt mindre exponerade för sexuellt och könsbaserat våld och katastrofrisker genom hållbar tillgång till renare matlagningsbränsle, förbättrad naturresursförvaltning och grön kompetensutveckling och försörjning. I fas 2 av SAFE+-programmet ansluter sig UNHCR och tar över från IOM som sammankallande organ för att stödja samordningen av FN:s gemensamma respons genom en så kallad "Pass-through and Parallel" administrativ struktur med gemensamma programmål integrerade i den övergripande humanitära Rohingyakrisens gemensamma responsplan (Joint Response Plan JRP) för 2022 och framåt.
SAFE+2 består av tre sammanlänkade strategiska prioriteringar som ska uppnås genom integrerade projekt som leds av FN-organen:
Mål 1: Tillgång till renare energi genom tillhandahållandet av gasol och energieffektiv matlagningsutrustning för att minska avskogningen och mildra klimatförändringarna.
Mål 2: Miljö och ekosystem kommer att fokusera på kunskapshantering relaterad till naturresurshantering och klimatåtgärder, ekosystemrehabilitering och miljövård för att stärka samhällets motståndskraft, mildra konflikter kring naturresurser, katastrofer och klimatchocker, samt synergier med gröna försörjningsmöjligheter, miljömedvetenhet och stärkande av social sammanhållning mellan värd- och flyktingsamhällen.
Mål 3: Resiliens kommer att bidra till att stärka motståndskraften och befintliga försörjningskapaciteter och samtidigt förhindra ytterligare skador på miljön på grund av ohållbara jordbruksmetoder.

The first phase of SAFE+ officially ended in June 2022. In consultations with the GoB, donors and four UN agencies (UNHCR, IOM, WFP and FAO), a second phase of the joint UN programme has been developed to continue the good practices achieved by SAFE+ beyond 2022. The goal of the programme is for refugees and host communities to become more climate-resilient and food secure as well as less exposed to SGBV and disaster risks through sustained access to cleaner cooking energy, improved natural resource management and green skills development and livelihoods. In Phase 2 of the SAFE+ programme, UNHCR is joining the programme and is taking over from IOM as Convening Agency to support coordination of the UN Joint Response through a Pass-through and Parallel administrative structure with Joint Programme objectives integrated into the overall Rohingya Humanitarian Crisis Joint Response Plan (JRP) for 2022 and beyond.
SAFE+ 2 consists of three interlinked strategic priorities to be achieved through integrated projects led or co-led by the participating agencies:
Objective 1: Access to Cleaner Energy will focus on provision of cleaner and more efficient cooking energy sources through the continued provision of LPG and energy efficient cooking equipment to reduce deforestation and mitigate climate change.
Objective 2: Environment and Ecosystems will focus on knowledge management related to watershed and natural resources management and climate action, ecosystem rehabilitation and environmental conservation to strengthen community resilience to mitigate conflicts over natural resources, disaster and climate shocks such as landslide risks, floods, and droughts through Nature-Based Solutions, as well as synergies with green livelihoods, environmental awareness and strengthening social cohesion between host and refugee communities.
Objective 3: Resilience will contribute to strengthening resilience and existing livelihoods capacities while preventing further harm to the environment due to the negative coping strategies and unsustainable agriculture practices. It will similarly ensure interventions in the camps are environmentally sound and refugees can be as self-sufficient as possible.

The Safe Access to Fuel and Energy Plus (SAFE2) programme objectives are to enable Rohingya refugees in the Cox's Bazar district to access cleaner energy, support the region's environment and ecosystems, and provide skills development and livelihoods to refugees and Bangladeshi host communities. The programme is currently in its second phase (July 2022-March 2025) and builds upon successes and lessons learned that were obtained during the programme's first phase (January 2019-June 2022). The SAFE2 programme is jointly implemented by FAO, IOM, UNHCR and WFP. The following results were reported in the 2023 report and the midterm evaluation:
1) Access to Cleaner Energy UNHCR and IOM have ensured that all Rohingya households have received regular 12 kg LPG refills throughout the year. Through this, LPG distribution has saved 13,390 hectares of forest (based on the Bangladesh Forest Inventory in 2017). Additionally, the use of LPG has caused a reduction of 375,300 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually, based on the methodology adopted by the 2019 Stanford University study on the human health and environmental costs and benefits of LPG vs firewood for cooking in the Rohingya camps.
According to the midterm evaluation, the impact of LPG provision on the daily lives of Rohingya households is reduced cooking time (84%), a neat and clean kitchen (71.1%), low cost (68.7%), no need to collect firewood (59.5%), painless cooking with reduced health problems (57.6%), and increased safety (54%). Deforestation has also decreased due to using LPG instead of firewood for cooking purposes.
2) Environment and Ecosystems WFP and IOM with technical support from FAO have planted trees covering 105 hectares of land (32 in 2022 and 73 in 2023) engaging community people through Cash-for-Work. As a result, 11.69% of the environment and ecosystems have been rehabilitated.
About 5.9% of the Rohingya community is engaged in the maintenance of tree plantations at a minimum cost of wages. Now, they are becoming aware of the direct and indirect benefits of forest conservation and protection. In response to the impact of forest conservation on their day-to-day life, Rohingya mentioned many benefits like providing shade (88.3%), cooler temperatures (68.8%), landslide risk mitigation (34.1%), minimising cyclone damage (34.4%), providing fruits (33.6%), and herbal medicine (23.8%). The Department of Forest has helped the programme develop a land stabilization method, promoting the plantation of various fast-growing indigenous species and replant in the area, which was previously national forest land.
In collaboration with the South Forest and Coastal Forest Divisions of Cox's Bazar district, FAO distributed 100 metric tons of organic and inorganic fertilizer as well as 200,000 dry bamboos to eight nurseries to facilitate seed germination and seedling production.
The conflict between the host and the Rohingya community over natural resource extraction, use of water bodies, etc has decreased. Local leaders and Camp-in-Charges have taken initiatives to resolve conflicts that come up, engaging the relevant GoB authorities when and where needed. Further, the capacity of these communities to resolve conflicts has increased. As per the midterm evaluation, an average of 2.6 conflicts between the community and plantation protectors generally occurred per year, and 1.2 initiatives per conflict were carried out to resolve those conflicts. However, most (43.5%) of the conflicts were managed by the joint coordination between the host and Rohingya community and the government and camp, including the Camp-in-Charges.
3) Resilience Since the start of SAFE2, WFP has provided vocational skills training to 5,227 Rohingya (3,394 female and 1,833 male), aquaculture training to 500 Rohingya (412 female and 84 male) and FAO has provided homestead gardening training to 600 Rohingya women. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) and inclusive TVET catering for 1,500 refugees with disabilities has encompassed a wide array of skills including reusable sanitary napkin production, handicrafts, tailoring, mechanics, bamboo and wood repair, gas stove repair, solar panel maintenance, and plumbing. Under the guidance of the Livelihoods and Skills Development Sector (LSDS), curriculums for both TVET and inclusive TVET incorporated basic literacy, functional literacy in English, Burmese and numeracy alongside vocational and livelihood skills.
The training provided to host community farmers and producer (both males and females) has had a noteworthy impact on increasing agricultural production. As per the evaluation findings, 36.3% of farmers and producers successfully increased their production and market sales in 2023 compared to 2022. The increase in average agricultural production in 2023 (789 kg) is higher than in 2022 (749 kg), which is evidence of the impact of training for the host community. As per their reporting, the average price of this production was BDT 37,193 in 2023 as compared to BDT 21,329 in 2022.
